name: Zephyr Results Sync

# SFCC-751 Deliverable 2. Runs after every completed run of either workflow
# that can produce a BrowserStack build — QA (release/** PRs,
# e2e-browserstack) or Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)
# (develop-PR path, e2e-browserstack-preview.yml, split out 2026-08-25 to
# stop polling for Deploy Preview — see that workflow's own comment) — and
# syncs any BrowserStack Test Observability results tagged @zephyr:<KEY>
# to Zephyr Scale (DE-hosted — BrowserStack's native Zephyr integration
# can't reach it, see scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs's doc comment and
# .docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md). On a failing test it also
# files a Jira defect with evidence, since BrowserStack's own "Report a
# bug" flow is manual-UI-only — confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for
# automatic-on-failure filing.
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['QA', 'Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)']
    types: [completed]

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read # to download the build-name artifact from the triggering run

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Skip only a fully cancelled run — a triggering run that failed
    # elsewhere (e.g. unit-tests, or the develop-PR path's own PR/Jira-key
    # lookup) may still have a real BrowserStack build worth syncing. The
    # sync script itself no-ops cleanly if no build exists for this run
    # (e2e-browserstack is conditionally gated on both workflows, so most
    # runs won't have one).
    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'
    steps:
      # Deliberately NOT checked out at github.event.workflow_run.head_sha.
      # workflow_run jobs get real secrets regardless of who triggered the
      # original run — checking out and then executing a PR branch's own
      # version of scripts/*.mjs at that ref would let a modified script on
      # the branch exfiltrate BROWSERSTACK_*/ZEPHYR_*/JIRA_* directly
      # (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-25). No ref: means the
      # default branch, which is also the only ref GitHub ever evaluates a
      # workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition from — this job
      # could never have run against a PR branch's version of itself
      # anyway (see .claude/rules/testing.md), so this costs nothing.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # Must use the identical build name the triggering run's
      # e2e-browserstack job computed — not recompute it. This job checks
      # out develop (see above), while e2e-browserstack ran against the
      # PR's own branch; scripts/computeBuildName.mjs's output depends on
      # which @zephyr:-tagged spec files exist in the checkout, so a PR
      # that adds or renames one would get a different computed name here
      # than the triggering run got, and the build lookup below would miss
      # entirely until the PR merges (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly,
      # 2026-08-25, when this only had to account for qa.yml). Downloading
      # the exact string that run persisted removes the drift instead of
      # just documenting it — true for either triggering workflow.
      - name: Download build name artifact from the triggering run
        id: download-build-name
        continue-on-error: true # no artifact means e2e-browserstack didn't run for this run — normal
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: browserstack-build-name
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      # A missing artifact is only safe to shrug off when e2e-browserstack
      # never ran for this triggering run (nothing to sync either way). If
      # it DID run, a real BrowserStack build exists under the Jira-derived
      # name -- silently falling back to the run number would make
      # findBuild() miss it and report "nothing to sync" when there
      # actually is something, hiding a real test failure instead of
      # syncing it (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-25, against
      # qa.yml; the same check now covers e2e-browserstack-preview.yml too
      # since both workflows name the job identically).
      - name: Verify build-name availability when e2e-browserstack ran
        if: steps.download-build-name.outcome == 'failure'
        run: |
          CONCLUSION=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}/jobs" \
            --jq '.jobs[] | select(.name == "Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)") | .conclusion')
          if [[ -n "$CONCLUSION" && "$CONCLUSION" != "skipped" ]]; then
            echo "::error::e2e-browserstack ran (conclusion: $CONCLUSION) for this run but its build-name artifact could not be downloaded. Refusing to fall back to the run number, which could silently miss a real BrowserStack build. Investigate the artifact upload step in the triggering workflow."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "e2e-browserstack did not run (or was skipped) for this run -- the run-number fallback is safe, there's no real build to miss."
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Resolve build name
        id: build-name
        run: |
          if [[ -f browserstack-build-name.txt ]]; then
            NAME=$(cat browserstack-build-name.txt)
          else
            NAME="${{ github.event.workflow_run.run_number }}"
          fi
          echo "name=$NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Sync BrowserStack results to Zephyr Scale
        run: node scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs
        env:
          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}
          # Keep in sync with browserstack.yml's testObservabilityOptions.projectName.
          BROWSERSTACK_PROJECT_NAME: 'Zim Project'
          BROWSERSTACK_BUILD_NAME: 'Sprint-${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}'
          ZEPHYR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZEPHYR_API_KEY }}
          ZEPHYR_API_URL: ${{ secrets.ZEPHYR_API_URL }}
          JIRA_URL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_URL }}
          JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL }}
          JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN }}

      # could never have run against a PR branch's version of itself
      # anyway (see .claude/rules/testing.md), so this costs nothing.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # e2e-browserstack job computed — not recompute it. This job checks

      # than the triggering run got, and the build lookup below would miss
      # entirely until the PR merges (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly,
      # 2026-08-25, when this only had to account for qa.yml). Downloading
      # the exact string that run persisted removes the drift instead of
      # just documenting it — true for either triggering workflow.
      - name: Download build name artifact from the triggering run

        continue-on-error: true # no artifact means e2e-browserstack didn't run for this run — normal
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: browserstack-build-name
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      # never ran for this triggering run (nothing to sync either way). If
      # it DID run, a real BrowserStack build exists under the Jira-derived
      # name -- silently falling back to the run number would make
      # findBuild() miss it and report "nothing to sync" when there
      # actually is something, hiding a real test failure instead of
      # syncing it (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-25, against
      # qa.yml; the same check now covers e2e-browserstack-preview.yml too
      # since both workflows name the job identically).

          fi

        id: build-name
        run: |
          if [[ -f browserstack-build-name.txt ]]; then

          else
            NAME="${{ github.event.workflow_run.run_number }}"

        run: node scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs
        env:
          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}

          BROWSERSTACK_PROJECT_NAME: 'Zim Project'
          BROWSERSTACK_BUILD_NAME: 'Sprint-${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}'
          ZEPHYR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZEPHYR_API_KEY }}
          ZEPHYR_API_URL: ${{ secrets.ZEPHYR_API_URL }}
          JIRA_URL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_URL }}
          JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL }}
          JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN }}

# browserstack.yml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
# NOTE: named without a leading dot deliberately — browserstack-node-sdk
# searches upward from cwd for exactly `browserstack.yml`; a `.browserstack.yml`
# (this file's name until 2026-08-25) is never found, so every SDK-driven run
# fails at config resolution before any test executes. Confirmed via
# BrowserStack's own docs, and via a real CI failure on PR #61.
# BrowserStack Playwright SDK configuration for cross-browser regression
# Docs: https://www.browserstack.com/docs/automate/playwright/sdk-node

userName: ${BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME}
accessKey: ${BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY}

# Top-level buildName/projectName govern the classic Automate dashboard's
# build grouping — a different product from Test Observability below, which
# has its own separate projectName/buildName under testObservabilityOptions.
# Without this, Automate showed every run as "Untitled Build Run #N" even
# though testObservabilityOptions.buildName was set correctly (confirmed
# 2026-08-25). Keep both blocks' values in sync.
buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"
projectName: "Zim Project"

framework: playwright

# Zimmermann tests only
testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm

# `platforms:` (with browserName/browserVersion/os/osVersion), not the
# classic Automate/Selenium `browsers:` key (browser/browser_version/
# os/os_version) — the Playwright Node SDK only recognises the former.
# `browsers:` is silently ignored: the SDK finds zero configured
# platforms and every test falls through to a genuine local Playwright
# launch instead of one on BrowserStack's cloud, which fails outright
# in CI since no local browser binaries are installed there (that's
# the SDK's job, remotely) — confirmed against the SDK's own installed
# source (modifyPlaywrightConf.js only ever reads a `platforms` key)
# and BrowserStack's current docs, after every desktop/mobile spec
# failed this exact way on PR #61, 2026-08-25. Safari has no Playwright
# driver of its own — `playwright-webkit` is BrowserStack's mapping for
# testing WebKit-engine (Safari-equivalent) behaviour, same reasoning
# for `playwright-firefox`. `chrome`/`edge` run for real since Playwright
# drives them directly via CDP.
#
# This account's plan allows exactly ONE concurrent BrowserStack session
# (confirmed with the developer, 2026-08-26 — not the account's queue
# ceiling this time, its actual `team_parallel_sessions_max_allowed`).
# Every platform below therefore runs strictly sequentially — platform
# count is a direct multiplier on wall-clock time and cost, with zero
# parallelism benefit from adding more. That ruled out a broad "current
# device − 2 generations" matrix across iPhone/Samsung/Pixel (would have
# been 9 real-mobile platforms alone): on a 1-session plan, what a real
# device buys you is OS/engine-version coverage, not device-generation
# depth — an iPhone 15 and an iPhone 17 on the same iOS build render
# near-identically, so one current device per platform we can't get any
# other way beats three generations of one we can. Six platforms total:
# three real devices (the coverage nothing else in this pipeline can
# provide) plus the three desktop engines already established. Edge and
# a second desktop Chrome OS were cut entirely — same Chromium engine as
# the real Android devices below, lowest marginal value under a strict
# 1-session budget.
platforms:
  # AU / US primary desktop browser
  - os: OS X
    osVersion: Sonoma
    browserName: chrome
    browserVersion: latest

  # AU / US / HK significant Safari share (Apple-heavy luxury market) —
  # desktop WebKit signal, distinct from the real iOS Safari device below
  # (different rendering path: desktop vs. mobile Safari).
  - os: OS X
    osVersion: Sonoma
    browserName: playwright-webkit
    browserVersion: latest

  # UK / EU / ME — the other non-Chromium desktop engine.
  - os: Windows
    osVersion: 11
    browserName: playwright-firefox
    browserVersion: latest

  # Real iOS device, real Safari — not Playwright's desktop WebKit build
  # (the entry above), which is a genuine engine but not the same
  # rendering path as Mobile Safari (different scrolling, fixed-position,
  # and viewport behaviour). BrowserStack added real-device Playwright
  # Safari support industry-first, June 2025 — confirmed current via
  # browserstack.com/guide/playwright-ios-automation and BrowserStack's
  # own docs (2026-08-26). Current model, iPhone 17, on its ship OS,
  # iOS 26 (confirmed live via web search, not training data — iPhone 17
  # launched Sept 2025 with iOS 26 pre-installed). deviceName + osVersion
  # + browserName: safari + realMobile: true is BrowserStack's documented
  # real-device shape (no `os:` field, matching the Android entries'
  # shape below) — not yet live-verified against this account's actual
  # device catalogue (local `.env` BrowserStack creds are blank, so this
  # couldn't be checked from here); confirm on the next real CI run.
  - deviceName: iPhone 17
    osVersion: '26'
    browserName: safari
    realMobile: true

  # Real Android device, Samsung — Samsung's One UI skin/GPU stack is a
  # meaningfully different rendering environment from stock Android.
  # Current model, Galaxy S26, on its ship OS: Android 16 / One UI 8.5
  # (confirmed live via web search, 2026-08-26). Not yet live-verified
  # against the device catalogue, same caveat as above.
  - deviceName: Samsung Galaxy S26
    osVersion: '16.0'
    browserName: chrome
    realMobile: true

  # Real Android device, Pixel — stock Android reference device, the
  # other real-world Android profile Zimmermann's Android traffic splits
  # across alongside Samsung. Current model, Pixel 11, on its ship OS:
  # Android 17 (confirmed live via web search, 2026-08-26) — launched
  # 2026-08-20, six days before this config was written, so there's a
  # real chance BrowserStack hasn't onboarded physical units yet; if the
  # next CI run can't find this device, fall back to Pixel 10 (Android 16)
  # until BrowserStack's catalogue catches up.
  - deviceName: Pixel 11
    osVersion: '17.0'
    browserName: chrome
    realMobile: true

# BrowserStack Test Observability — collects per-test results/tags, read by
# .github/workflows/zephyr-results-sync.yml (SFCC-751) to sync Zephyr Scale
# execution records. Not BrowserStack's native Zephyr link — that only
# supports US/EU API regions and this org's Zephyr instance is DE-hosted, so
# results are synced via our own workflow instead. projectName matches the
# real BrowserStack project ("Zim Project", id 2664550) — confirmed via a
# live GET /ext/v1/projects call on 2026-08-25 that no "Zimmermann-PWA"
# project exists in this account.
testObservability: true
testObservabilityOptions:
  projectName: "Zim Project"
  buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"

# This account's plan allows exactly 1 concurrent BrowserStack session
# (confirmed with the developer, 2026-08-26) — parallelsPerPlatform can
# only ever be 1 here; anything higher requests more concurrent sessions
# than the plan allows and risks [BROWSERSTACK_QUEUE_SIZE_EXCEEDED] again
# (first hit at 10 concurrent, 2026-08-25, when this was 5 platforms x 2).
# With 1 concurrent session, all 6 platforms above run strictly
# sequentially regardless of this value — see the platforms: comment for
# why platform count, not parallelism, is now the real cost/time lever.
parallelsPerPlatform: 1

Here is the structural map of the pipeline introduced by PR #61.

---

## 1. Trigger Map

| Workflow | Trigger | Jobs (dependency order) |
|---|---|---|
| `qa.yml` | `pull_request` → `develop` or `release/**` | `detect-changes` (no deps) → `unit-tests`, `storybook-test` (need `detect-changes`) → `e2e-localhost`, `e2e-browserstack` (need `unit-tests` + `detect-changes`) |
| `deploy-preview.yml` (new) | `push` to `feature/**` or `fix/**` (excludes `fix/release-*`, `fix/release/**`) | `deploy-preview` (single job, no deps) |
| `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` (new) | `workflow_run`: workflow `Deploy Preview`, type `completed` | `e2e-browserstack` (single job, no deps) |
| `zephyr-results-sync.yml` | `workflow_run`: workflows `QA` or `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)`, type `completed` | `sync` (single job, no deps) |
| `protected-file-guard.yml` | `pull_request` → `develop`, `main`, `release/**`; types `opened / synchronize / reopened` | `branch-target-guard` (no deps), `file-tier-checks` (no deps) — run in parallel |

---

## 2. Per-Job `if:` Conditions and Skip / Zero-Test Paths

### qa.yml — `detect-changes`

No `if:`. Always runs. Produces four outputs used downstream: `e2e`, `vitest`, `storybook`, `e2e_scope`, `jira_keys`. Also uploads artifact `e2e-scope.json` consumed by `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`.

Scope logic (qa.yml lines 148–171):
- If base ref is `release/*` → `e2e_scope=full`
- If no e2e-relevant files changed → `e2e_scope=skip`
- If every e2e-relevant changed file is also in the `e2e_homepage` allow-list → `e2e_scope=homepage`
- Otherwise (shared/global path or unclaimed area) → `e2e_scope=skip`

### qa.yml — `unit-tests`

`if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.vitest == 'true'` (qa.yml line 246)

Skips when no file in `overrides/**`, `vitest.config.*`, `vitest.setup.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `babel.config.js` changed since the last remote commit AND runtime deps (the `dependencies` block of `package.json`) did not change.

### qa.yml — `storybook-test`

`if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.storybook == 'true'` (qa.yml line 389)

Skips when no file in `overrides/app/components/**`, `overrides/app/pages/**`, `overrides/app/hooks/**`, `overrides/app/theme/**`, `overrides/app/types/**`, `.storybook/**`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` changed since the last remote commit.

### qa.yml — `e2e-localhost`

```yaml
if: |
  !cancelled() &&
  needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
  needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e_scope != 'skip' &&
  (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped')
```
(qa.yml lines 462–466)

Skip paths:
1. Workflow cancelled.
2. No e2e-relevant path changed.
3. `e2e_scope == 'skip'` (diff touches paths outside every area's allow-list on a develop-PR).
4. `unit-tests` failed (not `success` and not `skipped`).

Zero-test path: When `e2e_scope == 'homepage'`, the run command is `npx playwright test --project=chromium --project=mobile-chrome --grep "@homepage"`. If the `--grep` matches no collected spec (e.g. all homepage specs are excluded by `testIgnore` on a project), Playwright exits 0 with zero tests. No explicit guard against a zero-match run exists.

### qa.yml — `e2e-browserstack` (release/\*\* only)

```yaml
if: |
  always() &&
  needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
  (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped') &&
  contains(github.base_ref, 'release/')
```
(qa.yml lines 605–609)

Skip paths: base ref does not contain `release/`; e2e not relevant; `unit-tests` failed. Note: `always()` means this runs even if `unit-tests` was skipped, but the explicit result check provides the actual gate.

The build name here is hardcoded to `github.run_number` (qa.yml line 629) — `computeBuildName.mjs` is not called from this job. `SPRINT_NUMBER` env var is set to the run number, which feeds `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"`.

### deploy-preview.yml — `deploy-preview`

No `if:`. Runs on every matching push (branch filter is in `on:`). `cancel-in-progress: false` on the concurrency group.

### e2e-browserstack-preview.yml — `e2e-browserstack`

Job-level: `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'`

Then a chain of per-step conditions:

1. "Find open PR for this branch" (always runs): sets `skip=true` → no further steps if no open PR found, or if the PR's base is not `develop`.
2. "Detect Jira story keys": only runs if `steps.pr.outputs.skip == 'false'`. If keys are empty, all downstream BrowserStack steps are skipped.
3. "Look up matching QA run": only runs if `steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''`.
4. "Download e2e-relevance artifact": only runs if `steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id != ''`; `continue-on-error: true`.
5. "Check e2e relevance": only runs if `steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''`. Sets `relevant=false` if the downloaded artifact says `e2e: "false"`. Fail-open: if the artifact could not be downloaded or read, defaults to `relevant=true`.
6. All remaining steps (build name, BrowserStack run) only execute if `steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'`.

Zero-test / zero-execution paths:
- Deploy Preview was cancelled → job skips entirely.
- No open PR for the pushed branch.
- PR base ref is not `develop`.
- No `SFCC-NNN` key anywhere in PR title, body, or branch name.
- `e2e-scope.json` downloaded from the QA run says `e2e: "false"`.
- `--grep` built from Jira keys (e.g. `@SFCC-751`) matches no collected spec.

### zephyr-results-sync.yml — `sync`

`if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'` (zephyr-results-sync.yml line ~42)

Zero-sync path (exits 0): If no BrowserStack build named `Sprint-{name}` exists in the project, the script logs "No BrowserStack build found — nothing to sync" and returns normally (script line ~259–262). This is the expected path for most QA runs where `e2e-browserstack` was skipped.

---

## 3. Secrets / Env Vars and Absent-Value Behaviour

### qa.yml — `e2e-localhost` (environment: `dev`)

| Name | Type | Effect if absent/empty |
|---|---|---|
| `PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET` | Secret | Dev server cannot authenticate with SLAS; server likely starts but all auth-gated API calls fail |
| `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID` | `vars` (dev env) | Dev server config missing; SFCC API calls fail |
| `COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID` | `vars` (dev env) | Same |
| `COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE` | `vars` (dev env) | Same |
| `COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID` | `vars` (dev env) | Same |
| `PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL` / `PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD` | Secret | Tests requiring a logged-in user fail |
| `E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU` etc. | Secret | Tests using those SKUs fail |
| `SITE_ID` | Hardcoded `au` | — |

### qa.yml — `e2e-browserstack` (environment: `test`)

| Name | Type | Effect if absent/empty |
|---|---|---|
| `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME` / `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY` | Secret | SDK auth fails; all tests fail immediately |
| `RETAIL_APP_HOME` | `vars` (test env) | `BasePage.goto()` resolves to empty string, all `page.goto()` calls use bare path; BrowserStack remote browsers get `http://localhost:3000/...` which they cannot reach → `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`. Documented as a real past failure (qa.yml lines 598–602). |
| `E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME` / `E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE` | Secret | Requests to the access-gated test tier are rejected before pages load |
| `SPRINT_NUMBER` | Set from `steps.build-name.outputs.name` (run number) | Not a secret risk; only affects BrowserStack build display name |

### e2e-browserstack-preview.yml (environment: `test`)

| Name | Type | Effect if absent/empty |
|---|---|---|
| `JIRA_URL` / `JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL` / `JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN` | Secret | `computeBuildName.mjs` falls back to `unknown-{key}` and exits 0 — BrowserStack run still proceeds with that degraded build name |
| `BROWSERSTACK_*` | Secret | Same as above |
| `RETAIL_APP_HOME` | `vars` (test env) | Used as fallback if the MRT preview hostname artifact is unavailable; same `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` risk |
| `E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME` / `E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE` | Secret | Sent to both the preview target and the fallback test tier; missing → access-gated requests rejected |

### zephyr-results-sync.yml

| Name | Type | Effect if absent/empty |
|---|---|---|
| `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME` / `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY` | Secret | `die()` → non-zero exit, step fails |
| `BROWSERSTACK_PROJECT_NAME` | Hardcoded env `'Zim Project'` | — |
| `BROWSERSTACK_BUILD_NAME` | Derived from artifact or run number | Empty string → `die()` (missing required env var check, script lines ~60–63) |
| `ZEPHYR_API_KEY` / `ZEPHYR_API_URL` | Secret | `die()` → non-zero exit |
| `JIRA_URL` / `JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL` / `JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN` | Secret | `die()` → non-zero exit |

Note: `ZEPHYR_API_URL` is expected to end in `/testcases` or `/testcases/` — the script derives `ZEPHYR_TESTEXECUTIONS_URL` by replacing that suffix with `/testexecutions` (script line ~87). If the URL does not match that pattern, the replace is a no-op and both URLs would be identical, causing Zephyr execution POSTs to hit the wrong endpoint.

### deploy-preview.yml

| Name | Type | Effect if absent/empty |
|---|---|---|
| `MRT_USER` / `MRT_API_KEY` | Secret | MRT API calls fail (target create/PATCH/push) |
| `GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN` | Secret | Cannot fetch GitHub Environment variables; env-var sync step fails |
| `github.token` | Automatic | Used for PR comment upsert |

---

## 4. `zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` — Inputs, Outputs, HTTP Calls, Error Behaviour

**File**: `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` (359 lines)

**Inputs**: Nine required env vars checked at startup (lines ~60–63); if any is absent, `die()` is called immediately. Also reads `GITHUB_SERVER_URL`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (all auto-provided by Actions).

**Outputs**: Writes a Markdown summary table to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Exits 0 on success or normal no-op; exits non-zero on fatal errors.

**External HTTP calls** (all via a `fetchJson` wrapper that throws on non-2xx):

1. `GET https://api-automation.browserstack.com/ext/v1/projects` — paginated; finds BrowserStack project by name.
2. `GET https://api-automation.browserstack.com/ext/v1/projects/{id}/builds?unique_build_names={buildName}` — finds the build for this run.
3. `GET https://api-automation.browserstack.com/ext/v1/builds/{buildId}/testRuns` — paginated; walks `hierarchy[].children[].details` to extract per-test name, tags, status, session URL, and failure logs.
4. `POST {ZEPHYR_TESTEXECUTIONS_URL}` — one call per test carrying a `@zephyr:` tag; creates a Zephyr Scale execution record.
5. `GET {JIRA_URL}/rest/api/3/issue/{storyKey}?fields=assignee` — reads assignee of the related story (for defect auto-assignment).
6. `GET {JIRA_URL}/rest/api/3/user/search?query={email}` — resolves a git committer email to a Jira account ID (fallback when story has no assignee).
7. `POST {JIRA_URL}/rest/api/3/issue` — files a Bug issue on every failed test that also has an `@SFCC-NNN` story tag.

**BrowserStack tag stripping**: The API returns tags without the leading `@` (e.g. `zephyr:SFCC-T285`, not `@zephyr:SFCC-T285`). The `zephyrKeyTag` and `storyKeyTag` functions account for this (script lines ~153–160).

**Error/exit behaviour**:
- `die(msg)` → `process.exit(1)`: on missing required env var; BrowserStack project not found; any unhandled rejection in `main()`.
- `warn(msg)` → `console.error('::warning::...')`, execution continues: per-test Zephyr POST failure; Jira assignee lookup failure; git blame fallback failure; Jira account-ID resolution failure; Jira defect creation failure. A failure on one test does not stop processing of subsequent tests.
- Normal exit 0: no build found for this run (expected for most QA runs where BrowserStack didn't execute); build found but zero tests carry a `@zephyr:` tag; all tests processed successfully.

**Not yet live-verified** (explicitly noted in the script's doc comment, line ~46): the `hierarchy[]` response shape from the BrowserStack Get Tests API has never been exercised against a real build payload in this account.

---

## 5. `computeBuildName.mjs` — Inputs, Output, Callers

**File**: `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs`

**Inputs**:
- CLI arg `<JIRA_KEY>` (required; exits 1 if absent).
- Env vars: `JIRA_URL`, `JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL`, `JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN` (if any are missing, falls back gracefully).

**HTTP call**: `GET {JIRA_URL}/rest/api/3/issue/{jiraKey}?fields=summary,customfield_10020` — reads the issue summary and sprint field. Auth via Basic.

**Local exec**: `grep -rlF "@{jiraKey}" --include=*.spec.js e2e/tests/zimm` to find specs tagged with the Jira key, then `grep -ohE "@zephyr:[A-Z]+-T[0-9]+"` on each matched file to extract Zephyr case keys.

**Output** (stdout only): A string of the form `{sprintNum}-{jiraKey}-{zephyrKey(s)} - {summary truncated to 40 chars}`, e.g. `3-SFCC-751-SFCC-T285 - QA Pipeline — Playwright spec…`. This string becomes the `SPRINT_NUMBER` env var, which is interpolated into `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"`.

**Fallback**: On any Jira HTTP error, prints `unknown-{jiraKey}` to stdout and exits 0. The BrowserStack run still proceeds; the build will be searchable but under a degraded name.

**Callers**:
- `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` "Compute build name" step (line: `NAME=$(node scripts/computeBuildName.mjs "$PRIMARY_KEY")` — only when `steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'`).
- `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` does **not** call this script. It uses `github.run_number` directly (qa.yml line 629).
- `zephyr-results-sync.yml` does **not** call this script. It downloads the artifact written by whichever BrowserStack job ran.

---

## 6. Spec Files

### `e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js`

**Tags**: `['@SFCC-751', '@homepage', '@p1', '@zephyr:SFCC-T285']` — participates in Zephyr Scale sync.

**Structure**: One `test.describe` block containing a `for...of` loop over `sitePrefixes` (imported from `e2e/fixtures/sitePrefixes`). Each iteration of the loop produces **one `test()` call**. The exact number of `test()` blocks is determined at runtime by the number of entries in `sitePrefixes`; the fixture file is not in scope here, so the count cannot be stated definitively.

**Assertion per test**: Navigates to the site's root URL via `ListMenuPage.goToSite()`, collects all relative `href` values from `#list-menu` links, and asserts: for a site with a `urlPrefix` (e.g. `/us`), every href either equals that prefix exactly or starts with `{prefix}/`; for the root-prefixed (no prefix) site, no href starts with any other site's prefix.

### `e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`

**Tags**: `['@SFCC-751', '@homepage', '@p1']` — no `@zephyr:` tag; **not** synced to Zephyr Scale.

**Structure**: One `test.describe` block with exactly **one `test()` block**.

**Assertion**: Opens the mobile hamburger drawer via `MobileDrawerMenuPage`, collects all relative hrefs from the drawer, filters to those containing `/category/`, and asserts `categoryHrefs.length > 0`. The spec file explicitly documents this test is **expected to fail** as of the PR date because the mobile drawer contains no category navigation links — it exists to make the gap visible in CI rather than assert passing behaviour.
